mainTopic: צירוף of consecrated items for מעילה, and whether קדשי מזבח have תורה-level מעילה according to רבי ינאי
overview: The משנה teaches that small amounts of different consecrated items combine to reach the minimum for מעילה. Altar items also combine for פיגול, נותר and טמא, and even altar items and בדק הבית items combine with each other for מעילה. The גמרא explains that the first clause is not extra, because it adds פיגול, נותר and טמא, which apply only to altar items. Then רבי ינאי says that מעילה applies only to בדק הבית items and an עולה, since the פסוק speaks of things that belong fully to ה׳. The גמרא challenges him from three משניות and a ברייתא, and each time answers that those sources speak of מעילה מדרבנן, with the פסוק in the ברייתא being only an אסמכתא. A statement of רבי יוחנן, that dead קדשים leave מעילה by תורה law, shows that living קדשי מזבח must have תורה-level מעילה. So the גמרא rereads the school of רבי ינאי: the פסוק of מעילה teaches only about בדק הבית, and קדשי מזבח get their מעילה from another source.

steps.title: The משנה: Which consecrated items combine together
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three combining rules: altar items with altar items (for מעילה and for פיגול, נותר, טמא), בדק הבית items with each other, and altar items with בדק הבית items (for מעילה).
steps.simpleTranslation: Items consecrated for the altar combine with each other to reach the amount needed for מעילה, and to make a person liable for פיגול, נותר and eating while טמא. Items consecrated for בדק הבית combine with each other. Altar items and בדק הבית items also combine with each other for מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה teaches that small amounts of different consecrated items can be added together to reach the minimum amount that makes a person liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For מעילה the minimum is a פרוטה's worth of benefit, and for פיגול, נותר and טמא the minimum is a כזית. The משנה says these amounts can be built up from different consecrated items, even across the two big groups, altar items and בדק הבית items.

keyTerms.meaning: Items consecrated to be offered on the altar
Items consecrated for the upkeep of the בית המקדש
They combine together to reach the minimum amount
Wrongful personal use of consecrated property
Forbidden sacrificial meat: a disqualifying intention, meat left past its time, and eating while ritually impure

steps.whatToRemember: Three rules: altar items with altar items (for מעילה and for פיגול, נותר, טמא), בדק הבית items with each other, and both groups with each other (for מעילה only).

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ, מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה
phrases.english: Items consecrated for the altar combine with one another
for misuse, and to make one liable for them
phrases.notes: To be liable for מעילה you need a פרוטה's worth of benefit; this tells us small amounts can add up to that.

phrases.english: because of piggul, notar, and impurity.

phrases.aramaic: קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה.
phrases.english: Items consecrated for Temple maintenance combine with one another.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ וְאֶחָד קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת
phrases.english: Both altar-consecrated items and Temple-maintenance items
combine with one another for misuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ, מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Altar items combine with each other for מעילה and for פיגול, נותר, טמא; בדק הבית items combine with each other; and the two groups combine with each other for מעילה.

steps.title: Why teach that altar items combine with each other?
steps.stepSummary: The last clause already teaches that items with very different kinds of sanctity combine, so the first clause about altar items with altar items seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last clause says that altar items and בדק הבית items combine, even though one has קדושת הגוף and the other has קדושת דמים. If so, do we really need to be told that altar items combine with other altar items?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the structure of the משנה: the first clause seems unnecessary because the last clause already teaches something stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Altar items are holy in their very body (קדושת הגוף), while בדק הבית items are holy only for their value (קדושת דמים). If even these two different kinds combine, then two altar items, which share the same kind of sanctity, should obviously combine. So why state it?

keyTerms.meaning: Sanctity of the item itself, as with an animal for the altar
Sanctity of the item's value only, as with בדק הבית property
Is it necessary to say? (it should be obvious)
Even so

phrases.english: GEMARA: Now, since one can say that it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: ״אֶחָד קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ וְאֶחָד קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת״
phrases.english: "Both altar items and Temple-maintenance items"
where this one has inherent sanctity
and that one has sanctity of value,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי קָתָנֵי: ״מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה״.
phrases.english: and even so it teaches: "they combine with one another."
Is it necessary to teach "altar items with altar items"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the first clause of the משנה is needed
steps.kashyaTarget: The first clause of the משנה (altar items combine with altar items)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר logic: if items with different kinds of sanctity combine, items with the same kind surely do, so the first clause is redundant.

steps.title: The first clause is needed for פיגול, נותר and טמא
steps.stepSummary: The first clause is needed because it also teaches combining for פיגול, נותר and טמא, which do not apply to בדק הבית items, so it has to stand as its own clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed because the first clause also teaches that they combine to make one liable for פיגול, נותר and טמא. These laws do not exist for בדק הבית items, so the תנא had to teach the altar case separately.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the first clause teaches something the last clause cannot, so it is not extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last clause covers only מעילה, because פיגול, נותר and טמא are laws about sacrifices and have nothing to do with בדק הבית property. The new point of the first clause is combining for those three איסורים, which only an altar-only clause can teach. That is why the תנא separated the clauses.

keyTerms.meaning: He separates it (teaches it as its own clause)
This does not apply there

steps.whatToRemember: The first clause is not redundant: its new point is combining for פיגול, נותר and טמא, which apply only to altar items.

phrases.english: Because it teaches about it
"to make one liable for them because of piggul, notar, and impurity,"

phrases.aramaic: דְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת לָא אִיכָּא הָכִי,
phrases.english: and with Temple-maintenance items this does not apply,
for that reason he separates it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the clause has a unique teaching (פיגול, נותר, טמא) that the other clause cannot include
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first clause seemed to teach only combining for מעילה, which the last clause already covers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause is needed for combining for פיגול, נותר and טמא, which apply only to altar items.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: מעילה applies only to בדק הבית items and an עולה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי states clearly that one is liable for מעילה only for בדק הבית items and an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: It is clear that one is liable for מעילה only for בדק הבית items and an עולה alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רבי ינאי that narrows which consecrated items carry מעילה liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה talked about מעילה for altar items in general, but רבי ינאי limits liability to two things: בדק הבית items and an עולה. The word מחוורתא shows he sees this as a clear, settled point. The גמרא will next ask for his source.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear
Burnt offering, completely burned on the altar
Only, alone

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying other sacrifices have no holiness at all. רבי ינאי is only limiting which items bring liability for מעילה, and the גמרא is about to show the source for that limit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said: It is clear,
one is not liable for misuse

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת וְעוֹלָה בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: except for Temple-maintenance items and a burnt offering alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about which items carry מעילה liability
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for מעילה applies only to בדק הבית items and an עולה.

steps.title: What is רבי ינאי's source? The פסוק begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי ינאי's rule and starts quoting the פסוק that is the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the פסוק says: "If a person commits מעילה against the holy things of ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי ינאי's source and begins to answer from a פסוק. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is the פסוק about the קרבן for מעילה, which speaks of "the holy things of ה׳." The next step explains how these words limit מעילה to בדק הבית and an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Commits misuse
Against the holy things of ה׳

phrases.english: What is the reason? Because the verse says:
"If a person commits misuse against the holy things of the Lord,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for and begins giving the source of רבי ינאי's rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural reason for limiting מעילה to בדק הבית items and an עולה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer begins with the פסוק "נפש כי תמעל מעל מקדשי ה׳" and is completed in step 6.

steps.title: Only items that belong fully to ה׳ carry מעילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי's reason: the פסוק speaks of קדשים that belong only to ה׳. Most altar offerings have a share for the כהנים or the owners, so they are left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Holy items that belong only to ה׳ are subject to מעילה. But altar offerings have a share for the כהנים and a share for the owners, so they don't count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes giving the reason for רבי ינאי's rule. The פסוק is about things that belong completely to ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בדק הבית items and an עולה go entirely to ה׳, since an עולה is fully burned. Offerings like חטאת and אשם are partly eaten by the כהנים, and שלמים are partly eaten by the owners. Because they are not 'uniquely for ה׳', the תורה's law of מעילה does not cover them.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy items that belong only to ה׳
Using holy property for personal benefit
Items consecrated to be offered on the altar
The owners who brought the offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This reason is what all the following challenges (steps 7–19) push against. In the end (step 20) the גמרא rereads רבי ינאי's school, so that the פסוק only limits what we learn from it, not the law of מעילה itself.

phrases.english: Holy items that are uniquely for ה׳
phrases.notes: This reads the words 'קדשי ה׳' in the פסוק about מעילה (ויקרא 5:15).

phrases.english: are subject to מעילה.
But items consecrated for the altar
have a share in them for the priests,
and have a share in them for the owners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by explaining the פסוק
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source and reason for רבי ינאי's rule
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קדשי ה׳ means items fully belonging to ה׳; altar offerings shared with כהנים or owners are excluded

steps.title: Challenge from our משנה: altar items combine for מעילה
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה says קדשי מזבח combine to reach the amount needed for מעילה. That suggests all altar offerings carry מעילה, not just an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: altar items combine with each other for מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ינאי from the משנה we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Combining only matters if each item can carry מעילה in the first place. The משנה speaks of all קדשי מזבח, not just עולות. So it seems to say that all altar offerings carry מעילה, against רבי ינאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Combine together to make up the minimum amount
With one another

phrases.english: We learned: items consecrated for the altar combine
phrases.notes: This is the first clause of our משנה, from step 1.

phrases.english: with one another for מעילה!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה לִמְעִילָה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's rule that only בדק הבית and עולה carry מעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה applies combining for מעילה to all altar items, which assumes they all carry מעילה

steps.title: Answer: that is only a rabbinic rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about מעילה מדרבנן. רבי ינאי was only speaking about the תורה law.
steps.simpleTranslation: By rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in one word: the משנה's מעילה is a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי's rule is about the תורה level. The חכמים added a rule of מעילה for other altar offerings, and that is the case the משנה is discussing. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, not from the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: 'מדרבנן' does not mean that using these offerings is allowed. It means the prohibition of מעילה here comes from the חכמים rather than the תורה.

phrases.english: By rabbinic law.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the source's law as rabbinic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows that all altar items carry מעילה from the תורה
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers to rabbinic מעילה; on the תורה level רבי ינאי stands

steps.title: Challenge: most-holy offerings slaughtered in the south
steps.stepSummary: Another משנה says one is liable for מעילה with קדשי קדשים slaughtered in the south. That group includes חטאת and אשם, not just an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: קדשי קדשים that were slaughtered in the south: one is liable for מעילה with them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second משנה that seems to go against רבי ינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשי קדשים include חטאת and אשם, which are partly eaten by כהנים. The משנה still says מעילה applies to them. That seems to contradict the rule that only items fully belonging to ה׳ carry מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the most holy level (עולה, חטאת, אשם)
The south side of the עזרה, the wrong place to slaughter these
One is liable for מעילה

phrases.english: Most-holy offerings that one slaughtered in the south
phrases.notes: This is from the first משנה of the מסכת. These offerings must be slaughtered in the north, so here they became invalid.

phrases.english: one is liable for מעילה with them!

steps.triggerLanguage: קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן בַּדָּרוֹם מוֹעֲלִים בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge of the same type as step 7
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה applies מעילה to חטאת and אשם, which are not fully for ה׳

steps.title: Same answer: a rabbinic rule
steps.stepSummary: Again the גמרא answers that this משנה is speaking about מעילה מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: By rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same one-word answer as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's ruling about offerings slaughtered in the south is a rabbinic rule. It does not show that the תורה law of מעילה covers חטאת and אשם.

phrases.english: By rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 the same way step 8 answered step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the source's law as rabbinic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קדשי קדשים carry מעילה from the תורה
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers to rabbinic מעילה

steps.title: Challenge: benefiting from a live or dead חטאת
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says one who benefits from a חטאת is liable for מעילה. While it is alive, he must lower its value first. Once it is dead, any benefit is enough. This again applies מעילה to a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: one who benefits from a חטאת while it is alive is not liable for מעילה until he lowers its value. When it is dead, once he benefits any amount, he is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third משנה that applies מעילה to a חטאת, which is not an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The details of this משנה (alive versus dead) do not matter for the challenge. What matters is that the משנה says 'מעל' about a חטאת at all. That seems to go against רבי ינאי.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gets benefit
A sin offering
That he lowers (damages) its value
Any amount at all

phrases.english: We learned: one who benefits from a sin offering
while it is alive has not committed מעילה
until he lowers its value.
When it is dead, once he has benefited
any amount, he has committed מעילה!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: הַנֶּהֱנֶה מִן הַחַטָּאת כְּשֶׁהִיא חַיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge of the same type
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules מעילה for a חטאת, which is not fully for ה׳

steps.title: Same answer again: a rabbinic rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again answers that this משנה speaks of מעילה מדרבנן. All three challenges are answered, and רבי ינאי's rule stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: By rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the third challenge exactly like the first two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules about a live or dead חטאת are a rabbinic version of מעילה. On the תורה level, מעילה still applies only to בדק הבית and an עולה.
steps.whatToRemember: For now, the גמרא reads רבי ינאי as holding that תורה-level מעילה applies only to בדק הבית and an עולה, so it explains every משנה that applies מעילה to other altar offerings as מדרבנן. Step 20 drops this reading: there, רבי ינאי's school only says that this one פסוק does not teach about קדשי מזבח.

phrases.english: By rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 the same way as steps 8 and 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the source's law as rabbinic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A חטאת carries מעילה from the תורה
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה refers to rabbinic מעילה; רבי ינאי's rule holds

steps.title: A ברייתא derives מעילה for altar portions from a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether there is really no תורה-level מעילה for altar sacrifices, since רבי learns from 'כל חלב לה׳' that the אימורים of קדשים קלים are subject to מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really no תורה-level מעילה? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי says: 'All the fat is to ה׳' comes to include the altar portions of קדשים קלים in the law of מעילה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that קדשי מזבח have no Torah-level מעילה. It quotes a ברייתא that learns מעילה for them from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now each challenge was a משנה, and the גמרא could say it meant מדרבנן. Here רבי bases the law on a פסוק, which sounds like a real תורה law. That makes the 'מדרבנן' answer harder to use.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
'All the fat is to ה׳' (ויקרא 3:16), the פסוק רבי learns from
The parts of a sacrifice that are burned on the altar
Sacrifices of lesser holiness, like a שלמים
To include

phrases.english: And by Torah law, is there not [מעילה]?
phrases.notes: This is asking about רבי ינאי's position that altar sacrifices have no Torah-level מעילה.

phrases.english: But it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי says:
"All the fat is to the Lord"
to include the altar portions of lesser-holiness sacrifices in מעילה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After three challenges were answered with 'מדרבנן', a stronger challenge comes from a source that uses a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's rule, and the repeated answer that these sources mean מעילה מדרבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A law learned from a פסוק sounds like a Torah law, so there seems to be Torah-level מעילה for קדשי מזבח.

steps.title: This too is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי's ruling is also מעילה מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer it gave before. The ברייתא is speaking about מעילה by rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא keeps its approach from steps 8, 10 and 12. But this source quotes a פסוק, so the answer will immediately be questioned.

phrases.english: By rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי's ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the law's level, from Torah to rabbinic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's ruling is a Torah law of מעילה for קדשי מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מעילה in the ברייתא is only rabbinic.

steps.title: But he quotes a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא brings a פסוק as its source, so how can it be only rabbinic?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he takes it from a verse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. A law that comes from a פסוק seems to be a תורה law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weak spot in the 'מדרבנן' answer is that רבי clearly learns the law from 'כל חלב לה׳'. The גמרא wants to know how a rabbinic law can have a פסוק as its source.

keyTerms.meaning: A verse
He takes it, learns it from

phrases.english: But he takes it from a verse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer just given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא means מעילה מדרבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bringing a פסוק as the source shows the law is from the Torah.

steps.title: The פסוק is only a support
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is an אסמכתא, a hint the רבנן attached to their own law, not its real source.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is merely a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the פסוק is only an אסמכתא. The law really comes from the רבנן, and the פסוק is just a hint attached to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes the חכמים connect a rabbinic law to a פסוק as a memory aid or support, even though the תורה itself does not demand it. Quoting a פסוק therefore does not prove a law is from the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק used as a support or hint for a rabbinic law, not as its real source
Merely, just

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that every law tied to a פסוק is a תורה law. An אסמכתא looks like a derivation, but the law itself is only rabbinic.

phrases.english: It is merely a support.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Downgrading the פסוק to an אסמכתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a פסוק is quoted, the law must be from the Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is only a support and the מעילה is rabbinic, so for now רבי ינאי's rule survives. The next challenge (step 17) presses further.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: dead קדשים leave Torah-level מעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings עולא quoting רבי יוחנן, who says קדשים that died are no longer subject to מעילה by תורה law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: consecrated animals that died have left the law of מעילה by תורה law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge from a statement of רבי יוחנן. It is setting up a careful reading of this statement in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying that dead animals 'leave' תורה-level מעילה implies that before they died they had תורה-level מעילה. The next steps work out which kind of קדשים he means.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated animals that died
They have left the law of מעילה
By Torah law

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר עוּלָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But didn't עולא say that רבי יוחנן said:
Consecrated animals that died
have left the law of מעילה by Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר עוּלָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא is answered, a new challenge comes from an אמורא's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's rule that קדשי מזבח have no Torah-level מעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If death removes Torah-level מעילה, then the animals had Torah-level מעילה while they were alive.

steps.title: Which קדשים is he talking about? Not בדק הבית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of קדשים רבי יוחנן means, and rules out קדשי בדק הבית, since even a garbage heap given to בדק הבית has מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he talking about? If you say items given to בדק הבית, they have מעילה even when dead. At worst it is like someone who gave a garbage heap to בדק הבית. Doesn't that have מעילה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which kind of holy animals רבי יוחנן means. It shows he cannot mean animals given to בדק הבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With בדק הבית, what is holy is the item's value, not its use on the altar. Even something worthless like a garbage heap carries מעילה once it is given. So a dead animal given to בדק הבית would still have מעילה, and רבי יוחנן's statement cannot be about them.

keyTerms.meaning: About what? What case is meant?
Items given for the upkeep of the בית המקדש
A garbage heap
It should be no worse than

phrases.english: About what [is he speaking]?
If you say about items given to Temple maintenance,
even when they die, also [there is מעילה],

phrases.aramaic: לָא יְהֵא אֶלָּא דְּאַקְדֵּישׁ אַשְׁפָּה לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: it should be no worse than one who gave a garbage heap to Temple maintenance;
phrases.notes: A dead animal is at least as valuable as a garbage heap.

phrases.english: doesn't it have מעילה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out what רבי יוחנן's statement in step 17 means, so the challenge can be sharpened.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which type of קדשים רבי יוחנן is speaking about
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not בדק הבית, because they keep מעילה even after death, just as a garbage heap does.

steps.title: So he means קדשי מזבח, which have Torah-level מעילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן must mean קדשי מזבח, which implies they have תורה-level מעילה while alive. The גמרא asks: according to רבי ינאי, do they have מעילה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he means קדשי מזבח, so they have מעילה by תורה law! Do they have מעילה [according to רבי ינאי]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רבי יוחנן is talking about altar sacrifices. That means they do have תורה-level מעילה while alive, which is a direct challenge to רבי ינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since בדק הבית was ruled out, only קדשי מזבח are left. If death takes them out of תורה-level מעילה, then they had it before. This contradicts רבי ינאי, who holds they have no תורה-level מעילה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals given to be brought as sacrifices on the altar
Do they have?

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge cannot be answered with 'מדרבנן', because רבי יוחנן himself says 'by תורה law'. So רבי ינאי's rule is under real pressure.

phrases.english: Rather, [he means] items given to the altar,
[so they have מעילה] by Torah law!
phrases.notes: While alive. Only then does it make sense to say death takes them out of it.

phrases.english: Do they have מעילה?
phrases.notes: He means: according to רבי ינאי, do they? He says they don't, so this is the problem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the clarification from step 18 and states the full challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's rule that קדשי מזבח have no Torah-level מעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's statement must be about קדשי מזבח, and it implies they have Torah-level מעילה while alive. That is the opposite of רבי ינאי's rule.

steps.title: Rereading the school of רבי ינאי: this verse teaches only about בדק הבית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its earlier reading of רבי ינאי's school. Their real claim is limited: the פסוק of מעילה teaches about קדשי בדק הבית, but קדשי מזבח are not learned from that specific פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what the school of רבי ינאי meant: from this verse we learn about things dedicated to בדק הבית. We do not learn about קדשי מזבח from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing what it thinks the school of רבי ינאי said. They never claimed that קדשי מזבח have only rabbinic מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רבי ינאי was quoted as holding that מעילה for קדשי מזבח is only rabbinic, which clashes with רבי יוחנן. The word אלא drops that version, and with it the repeated 'מדרבנן' answers of steps 8–16. The statement of רבי ינאי's school is only about the source: this one פסוק covers בדק הבית, while קדשי מזבח can have תורה-level מעילה from somewhere else, so there is no conflict with רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals that the earlier understanding is being dropped
Items dedicated for upkeep of the בית המקדש
Items, mainly animals, dedicated as קרבנות for the מזבח
We learn from it
Misusing הקדש for personal benefit, which brings a קרבן and payment

steps.confusionAlert: Saying "we do not learn קדשי מזבח from this פסוק" does not mean קדשי מזבח have no תורה-level מעילה. It only means that this פסוק is not their source.
steps.whyThisMatters: It brings רבי ינאי's school into agreement with רבי יוחנן: both now hold that קדשי מזבח have מעילה from the תורה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָכִי קָא אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: Rather, this is what the school of רבי ינאי says:
From this verse
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק about מעילה in ויקרא 5:15.

phrases.english: we learn about things dedicated to בדק הבית;
we do not learn from it about things dedicated to the מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכִי קָא אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19 by reinterpreting the position of רבי ינאי's school.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of an earlier statement: what looked like a claim about the level of the law is narrowed to a claim about the source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ינאי (as first quoted in step 4) held that קדשי מזבח have only rabbinic מעילה, against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: They only meant that this פסוק teaches about בדק הבית. קדשי מזבח still have תורה-level מעילה from another source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מעילה פסוק of ויקרא 5:15 is the source for קדשי בדק הבית, not for קדשי מזבח.
